label: Moral-governance source identity and intellect/will omission test
summary: Tested the #1747 proposed moral governance to source-level intellect and will on one fixed informed easy-rescue case (same actual necessary root n, weak moral-order grounding predicate, agents, obligations, standing and priority). Finite Boolean valuations witness that the weak, uninterpreted GroundsMoralOrder predicate, together with ActualRoot and NecessaryAt, entails neither HasIntellect(n) nor HasWill(n) in that signature; they are not countermodels of a strong authored-law premise; a distinct rational secondary governor g can coexist with impersonal n; knowledge of ends without will is compatible only when q19's existing WillFollowsIntellectReading is withheld; and HasWill plus intentional global ordering does not by itself give recipient-directed WillsGoodFor. Populated positive profile witnesses nonvacuity only for the selected predicate assignments. These are JS-checked structural omission controls, not Lean/Comparator certificates, actual-world models, or refutations of historical rivals. Wielenberg's primitive norms can reject the stronger 'n grounds all authoritative norms' premise instead of satisfying it; actual Darwall standing remains open. Aquinas ST I-II q90 a1 ad3, q91 and q93, and ST I q19 motivate a conditional source-lawgiving/practical-end-adoption route; q93 already assumes divine governance. Reused existing GodHasIntellect and GodHasWill consumers and the delivered modular q19 will result, with no new proof or root-premise status change. Independent semantic challenge accepted the conditional distinction with those explicit qualifications. Detailed connected reconstruction and rival comparison: docs/notes/moral-governance-intellect-will.md.
blocker: The actual-world moral grounding/identity adapter remains unproved: show that the same actual necessary root n, rather than a secondary rational governor g or an impersonal normative standard, understands the case's goods and itself promulgates an authoritative law for a justified common good. Actual end-adoption, creative selection, and recipient-specific willing have further open #1459/#1737 interfaces. Next test fixes one moral obligation and its claimant while comparing source-level representation/promulgation against only derivative rational recognition.
